notes: NCBI StatPearls Mixed Connective Tissue Disease, updated 2024-07-27, was reread for anti-U1-RNP, Raynaud/puffy digits, inflammatory arthritis and myositis overlap features, and the U1-RNP role in pre-mRNA maturation.
NLM/PMC U1-RNP review was reread for the normal spliceosomal function of U1 snRNP, including recognition of the 5′ splice site.
The official USMLE 2026 Multisystem page 33 was visually verified and explicitly lists mixed connective tissue disease.

blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

claim_audit.phenotype: MCTD combines Raynaud/puffy hands with overlapping inflammatory arthritis, myositis and other connective-tissue-disease features and is strongly associated with high-titer anti-U1-RNP.
claim_audit.antigen_function: U1 snRNP is a spliceosomal ribonucleoprotein that recognizes the 5′ splice site and participates in intron removal from pre-mRNA.
claim_audit.specificity_nuance: Anti-U1-RNP is required/characteristic in common MCTD criteria but is not exclusive to MCTD; the full clinical phenotype is therefore necessary.
claim_audit.distractors: DNA origin licensing, aminoacyl-tRNA charging, signal-recognition-particle targeting and ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis are distinct molecular processes not performed by U1 snRNP.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Raynaud phenomenon, puffy digits, inflammatory arthritis, proximal myositis and high-titer anti-U1-RNP form a classic MCTD overlap phenotype. The autoantigen is U1 snRNP, whose normal function is 5′ splice-site recognition and spliceosome assembly during pre-mRNA processing.
adversarial_second_pass.sle_challenge: Anti-U1-RNP can occur in SLE. However the item does not ask whether the antibody alone proves MCTD; the combined overlap phenotype supplies the clinical context.
adversarial_second_pass.antisynthetase_challenge: Inflammatory myositis could suggest antisynthetase syndrome, but the supplied anti-U1-RNP plus Raynaud/puffy-hand/polyarthritis overlap pattern is MCTD and the lead asks about the identified U1 antigen rather than disease classification alone.
adversarial_second_pass.molecular_distractor_check: Each wrong option is a real cellular process with a different molecular machine, preventing a trivial 'only RNA answer' cue.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: All options describe intracellular macromolecular processing functions at a comparable abstraction level.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No antibody titer threshold, prevalence, diagnostic-score cutoff or prognostic frequency is required.
